title: Markov length can diverge in systems whose universal physics is spatially Markovian
abstract: Conditional mutual information (CMI) probes spatial non-Markovianity and plays a central role in a recently developed framework for defining mixed-state phases based on local reversibility. This framework sharply distinguishes exponentially decaying from algebraically decaying CMI, since the latter obstructs equivalence to a state with finite Markov length. Here we show that states that flow to the same renormalization-group (RG) fixed point can nevertheless exhibit qualitatively different CMI. Starting from a critical Gibbs state of a finite-range local classical Hamiltonian, whose CMI vanishes beyond the interaction range, we show that an RG-irrelevant perturbation that breaks detailed balance generically generates algebraically decaying CMI. Crucially, these power-law tails are cutoff-suppressed: although they lead to an infinite Markov length at every fixed lattice cutoff, they vanish as a positive power of the cutoff in the continuum limit. We construct solvable models that exhibit this phenomenon and predict that the Ising-symmetric critical point of Toom's cellular automata generically exhibits such behavior. We also find analogous cutoff-suppressed CMI in the high-temperature paramagnetic phase of the long-range Ising paramagnet, in contrast with the genuine power-law CMI at the finite-temperature critical point in this same model that survives the continuum limit. We also derive a general result that in one spatial dimension, CMI decays faster than the inverse square of the buffer length if and only if the long-distance physics is Markovian.
summary: This work develops a framework using Conditional Mutual Information (CMI) to diagnose spatial non-Markovianity in physical systems. The authors demonstrate that even when systems flow to the same fixed point, perturbations can induce power-law CMI tails that are cutoff-suppressed. This provides a precise theoretical tool to distinguish between truly non-Markovian physics and artifacts of the lattice cutoff.
main_problem: The paper investigates how spatial non-Markovianity can be probed using Conditional Mutual Information (CMI) and distinguishes between different types of power-law decay in CMI.
main_result: It shows that irrelevant perturbations breaking detailed balance can generate cutoff-suppressed, algebraically decaying CMI, leading to an infinite Markov length at any finite lattice cutoff but vanishing in the continuum limit.
method: The analysis employs the Renormalization Group (RG) framework, perturbative expansions in the perturbation strength ($\epsilon$), and scaling arguments for Gaussian distributions.
model_or_system: The study analyzes critical Gibbs states of finite-range local classical Hamiltonians, using Langevin dynamics to model the time evolution. Specific examples include the Ising-symmetric critical point of Toom's cellular automata and the long-range Ising paramagnet.
key_observables: Conditional Mutual Information (CMI), Markov length ($\xi_M$), and the decay rate of CMI.
important_parameters: Lattice cutoff ($a$), perturbation strength ($\epsilon$), and relative length scales ($l, l_B, \xi_{	ext{cross}}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the CMI is UV-finite in the continuum limit and relies on the perturbation being RG-irrelevant.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the geometry of CMI calculation in both annular (2D) and 1D settings.
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining CMI to probing non-Markovianity, develops the RG framework for analyzing decay types, and applies these tools to specific models like the Ising paramagnet and Gaussian systems.
why_interesting: The rigorous connection between CMI decay rates and the underlying Markovian nature of the steady state is a powerful diagnostic tool for characterizing complex, non-equilibrium phases in statistical mechanics.
